payload.title: The stored image type is decided from the pixels, and nothing is stored twice
payload.context: Images review (#25): a photo saved as PNG was stored as a larger PNG that no platform takes, web-sized uploads grew, and the same file could be stored several times.
payload.rationale: Any transparent pixel means PNG. An opaque image from a lossless format up to 9 megapixels is encoded both ways and the smaller kept. Everything else is JPEG, never at a higher quality than its source. Animated PNG and WebP are refused like GIF. An upload whose stored bytes the workspace already holds returns the existing image.
payload.consequences: Screenshots stay sharp, photos fit the platforms, and a duplicate costs no quota. The quota is unlimited by default on a self-hosted instance.
